local_calendar.t: State law has every Colorado county except the two that are cities and counties, Denver and Broomfield, elect a clerk and recorder, treasurer, assessor, sheriff, coroner and surveyor on November 3, 2026, along with the county commissioners whose four-year terms are up; voters of the Regional Transportation District elect directors in seven of its fifteen director districts; and judges of the district courts, the county courts and Denver's juvenile and probate courts face a yes or no retention vote. School boards are elected in November of odd-numbered years and special district boards in May of odd-numbered years; towns regularly vote in April of even-numbered years and cities in November of odd-numbered years, unless a municipality's voters have moved its election to November of even-numbered years, in which case it shares this ballot. No district attorney is on the Secretary of State's 2026 list.

Ballot order is given only for the director contests whose order the Secretary of State drew by lot (District B, District K, District O); a retention vote has one name. A judicial district's counties are read from the statute, and a director district's from the Secretary of State's 2022 abstract of votes, the last time these director seats were on the ballot.
